behaviours.name: walk
behaviours.definition: Moves forward at a walking pace so the whole body changes place; at most one paw off the ground at a time.

behaviours.name: trot
behaviours.definition: Brisk gait with diagonal fore/hind pairs moving together; used for covering distance and exploring.

behaviours.name: run
behaviours.definition: Faster than walking, with moments where several paws are off the ground together.

behaviours.name: jump
behaviours.definition: Pushes off with the hind legs; either all four paws leave the ground or the forepaws are placed up on a wall/fence.
behaviours.species: domestic dog (shelter); Tibetan fox (pounce on prey)

behaviours.name: pacing
behaviours.definition: Repetitive walking along the same route with no apparent destination (a stereotypy; a sign of poor welfare, not a cozy idle).
behaviours.notes: Keep out of the hero's idle set.

behaviours.name: circling (repetitive)
behaviours.definition: Tracing the same circle more than three times in one direction (stereotypy). Distinct from the brief turn-around before lying down, for which no sourced number was found.

behaviours.name: carry/scatter object
behaviours.definition: Takes an object in the mouth and carries or scatters it around the enclosure.

behaviours.name: eat
behaviours.definition: Eats food provided in the enclosure.

behaviours.name: drink
behaviours.definition: Drinks from a bowl or water dispenser.

behaviours.name: chew/bite blanket or toy
behaviours.definition: Bites or mouths a blanket or toy (object play / chewing).

behaviours.name: dig
behaviours.definition: Repeatedly scrapes the ground with the forepaws, making a hole.

behaviours.name: dig/splash in water bowl
behaviours.definition: Puts one or both forepaws in the water bowl and paddles them back and forth, or plays in a pool.

behaviours.name: sniff ground/object
behaviours.definition: Head lowered to a surface or object, inhaling in quick sniffs.

behaviours.name: air sniff
behaviours.definition: Head raised toward a distant scent, sniffing the air.

behaviours.name: visual exploration (look around)
behaviours.definition: Watches particular objects inside or outside the enclosure (not other animals).
behaviours.notes: The most common awake state in the shelter dataset.

behaviours.name: scan
behaviours.definition: Stands or sits with the head raised, staring in one direction or sweeping back and forth; ears rotate.

behaviours.name: freeze
behaviours.definition: Stops suddenly mid-walk or mid-run and stays rigid; only the eyes and ears move.

behaviours.name: alert stand
behaviours.definition: Stands with limbs straight and body tense, tail down or slightly raised.

behaviours.name: lick object
behaviours.definition: Touches a scented object with the tongue.

behaviours.name: paw at object
behaviours.definition: Touches an object with one or both forepaws.

behaviours.name: paw lift
behaviours.definition: Lifts one foreleg and puts it down again, often several times quickly.

behaviours.name: lying, head down
behaviours.definition: Belly or side on the ground with the legs stretched out, tucked or to one side; head resting on the ground, an object or the paws; eyes open or closed.

behaviours.name: lying, head up
behaviours.definition: As above but with the head held up off the ground; eyes open or closed.

behaviours.name: curled up
behaviours.definition: Lying curled into a tight ball (a variant of the resting position).

behaviours.name: sit (inactive)
behaviours.definition: Hindquarters on the ground, forelegs straight and supporting the front; no other behaviour going on.

behaviours.name: stand (inactive)
behaviours.definition: All four feet on the ground, legs (nearly) straight; no other behaviour going on.

behaviours.name: sleep: drowsiness
behaviours.definition: Light, transitional sleep: eye movements slow down, muscle tone drops but is still present, breathing fairly regular.

behaviours.name: sleep: non-REM
behaviours.definition: Deep sleep: no or slight eye movement, regular breathing, lowered muscle tone.

behaviours.name: sleep: REM
behaviours.definition: Rapid eye movements, muscles go slack, breathing and heartbeat become irregular (the 'dreaming' twitch phase).

behaviours.name: self-groom
behaviours.definition: Grooms itself: licking, nibbling or scratching its own coat.

behaviours.name: body shake (shake-off)
behaviours.definition: Quick side-to-side twist of the whole body (full) or of the head only.
behaviours.notes: In a dog run/daycare most shakes (89%) fell at a switch between activities; treat as punctuation between idle states.

behaviours.name: stretch
behaviours.definition: Arches the body by pushing the forelegs out in front.

behaviours.name: roll on back
behaviours.definition: Lies on its back and wriggles the whole body in waves.

behaviours.name: scent roll
behaviours.definition: Lowers chin and neck to a smell, then rubs head, neck, shoulders and back into it.

behaviours.name: yawn
behaviours.definition: Opens the mouth wide for a few seconds while breathing out.

behaviours.name: lip lick
behaviours.definition: Shows part of the tongue and runs it along the upper lip (often a mild stress signal).

behaviours.name: sneeze
behaviours.definition: Deep breath in then a sudden forced breath out through the nose.

behaviours.name: pant (modifier)
behaviours.definition: Open-mouth fast breathing; recorded as a modifier because heat causes it too.

behaviours.name: urinate
behaviours.definition: Passes urine.

behaviours.name: defecate
behaviours.definition: Passes faeces.

behaviours.name: tail wag
behaviours.definition: Tail swings side to side repeatedly.

behaviours.name: bark
behaviours.definition: Mouth snaps open and shut, giving short low sounds, often in a series.

behaviours.name: howl
behaviours.definition: Long, medium-pitched call with the muzzle pointed upward.

behaviours.name: whine
behaviours.definition: Soft, high, whistling sound in short repeated bursts.

behaviours.name: yelp
behaviours.definition: High, loud, short cry; stronger than a whine.

behaviours.name: scent mark (urine/rub)
behaviours.definition: Sniffs the ground, then urinates on or rubs the body or tail against rocks, plants or objects.

behaviours.name: beg position
behaviours.definition: Lifts both forepaws together while the hind legs stay bent (sitting up).

behaviours.name: growl
behaviours.definition: Low threatening sound, often with teeth showing.

behaviours.name: negative interaction
behaviours.definition: Threatening exchange with a stiff or defensive posture.

behaviours.name: cower
behaviours.definition: Curls up or crouches low out of fear.

behaviours.name: tremble
behaviours.definition: Continuous shivering of the body or part of it.

behaviours.name: positive interaction
behaviours.definition: Friendly or playful exchange with another dog or person.

behaviours.name: solitary play
behaviours.definition: Plays alone or with a toy.

behaviours.name: play bow (full)
behaviours.definition: Front end drops so the elbows touch the ground while the hind legs stay standing; may wag and bark. A play signal.

behaviours.name: play bow (half)
behaviours.definition: Forelegs fold only halfway, elbows stay off the ground, hind legs standing.

behaviours.name: tail chasing
behaviours.definition: Spins in circles trying to bite its own tail (stereotypy when repeated).

behaviours.name: courtship / mating
behaviours.definition: Name only (cozy game; not modelled).

behaviours.name: den / shelter use
behaviours.definition: Repeatedly returns to the same spots to rest, raise young or socialise.

behaviours.name: out of sight
behaviours.definition: Animal not visible (behind objects, inside the doghouse).
